set.st: Legend (Des Moines Register 1927): a lone Indian fleeing pursuers in 1832 with a heavy two-lobed sack of plunder crossed a clearing on what became the Christopher Meyer farm; at a spring about half a mile on he was seen without the sack and was later shot. Meyer built his house between the clearing and the spring and dug for years; his daughter Dora (Mrs. Timmerman) and the school children hunted the hummocks. Pin is the Meyer farm on the 1886 atlas, not the spot itself. The 1927 feature calls the place Brookman's Bluff.
set.pl: Christopher Meyer farm, NE¼ sec 10 T100N R5W, Union City Twp (1886 atlas), about 9 mi W of New Albin; the clearing and the spring half a mile on are not yet fixed; called Brookman's Bluff in the 1927 feature
